payload.assumptions_validated:
KILLER. Of the five ranked unknowns, three are closed by evidence, one is closed by reading the shipped code, and ONE IS DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN and bound to this iteration's own release.

U3 browser-side decryption - HOLDS, and the design CHANGED to make it hold. run-e8599b7b7d2a, 6/6. The change is not cosmetic: the payload layout (iv|tag|ct, rejoined as ct||tag for Web Crypto) and the base64url fragment key are now contract, and BOTH were wrong in my own earlier probe. Had the spike not run, the shipped page would have failed to decrypt on the owner's phone while every server-side check reported green - the same shape of failure as the untappable button this iteration exists to repair, caught this time before it reached a device.

U4 the wait signal - HOLDS, and the design CHANGED to a better mechanism than the one assumed. The assumption was that the announce path could be TOLD the run's intent. Reading bin/se-board.ts, it cannot: announce is driven by a 3s timer that sees only 'an offer exists'. The replacement needs no signal at all - se_wait { condition: { kind: 'offer' } } IS the act of waiting, so the trigger and the intent are the same event. A whitelist by construction: one named act publishes; everything else does not.

U1 the transport - HELD BEFORE THE ITERATION, run-bfd564ff9add, 7/7: encrypt, publish to KV, serve as text/html, read-after-write measured at 1067ms against the design's assumed ~60s, ciphertext-only at rest, and a three-action card with a view link accepted by ntfy.

U5 config read at announce time - not spiked, correctly: it is build work with no unknown in it.

U2 THE TAP AND THE RENDER - OPEN, AND THAT IS THE RULING. No agent-side evidence can close it: it needs the owner's thumb on a real device. It is not deferred into vagueness - it is bound as D1 to this iteration's gate_release, which the owner adjudicates from the phone. So the one assumption that cannot be validated by evidence is the one whose validation IS the release. Naming it plainly: if it fails there, this iteration does not ship.
payload.buildable:
YES, and more cheaply than at M5. THREE OF THE FOUR ELEMENTS ARE ALREADY PROVEN CODE rather than design intent: E2's crypto core is SP1's tested seal/open pair, E2's publish and serve legs are the probe's exercised calls, and E3's card shape is v1's shipped ask.go with the absolutization rule its own comment names. What is genuinely new is small and bounded - the page template that carries the ciphertext plus its inline decryptor, and the rewiring of the announce trigger from the board's timer to the park seam.

No element was added, split or merged during probing, so the M5 allocation stands unchanged and the build's chunks map onto it directly. The one interface that moved is E3's trigger, and it moved onto a call that already exists.

Buildable ALSO in the sense that matters for the tests: every leg has a way to be checked without a live topic or a live key. The crypto round-trips in-process, the ladder's degradation is provoked by injecting a failing brief pipeline, the absolutization is a pure function over a pairing, and the publish-iff-parking rule is observable at the seam. Only the final render-and-tap needs the outside world, and it is the demonstration, not a test.
payload.results_recorded:
Every spike pinned to its run, no result retyped from memory:

SP1 decryption round trip -> run-e8599b7b7d2a. 6/6: round trip over a 20k brief; wrong key throws; tampered ciphertext throws (GCM authenticates); wrong tag position throws; key charset url-safe; payload 26KB against KV's 25MB cap. Timebox 20 minutes, spent well under.

SP2 the wait signal -> no run ref, and that is honest: it was answered by READING the shipped code, not by executing anything. Sources: bin/se-board.ts (the phoneTick timer that owns the trigger today) and engine/wait.ts (seWait, the declared park). Recording it as a code-reading result rather than dressing it as an experiment.

U1 the transport -> run-bfd564ff9add, 7/7, predating the requirements gate.

PROMOTIONS MARKED, and marked as permanent rather than provisional: SP1's seal/open pair enters engine/brief.ts in substance unchanged; SP1's four negative checks become permanent tests, because they are the only guard between a shipped brief and a page that silently fails to decrypt; SP2's finding becomes both the wiring decision and the R9 acceptance check. Explicitly NOT promoted: the earlier throwaway probe script, which carried the two crypto defects SP1 found and must not be mistaken for a reference.

One out-of-band finding recorded rather than folded in: note-65857e4bd6e6, missing required-arg validation at tool dispatch, found by being fooled by it mid-spike. Routed to i9, does not block this build.
